So the build starts from the right assumptions.

What is this, shaped like?*

Mixed — it has a face and a programmable surface
Who can create short links?*

Decides the auth layer and what the rate limiter keys on (IP vs key vs account).

Anyone, anonymously
Only clients with an API key
Registered user accounts
Internal services only (trusted network)
Can callers choose their own short code (vanity URLs)?*

Changes the data model and collision handling.

No — always auto-generated
Yes — optional custom alias

Do links ever expire?*

Drives storage cleanup and what a hit on a dead link returns.

Never — permanent
Caller sets an optional expiry

What should be tracked when a short link is visited?*

Full logging adds a write on every redirect and possibly privacy obligations.

Nothing — just redirect
Total click count only
Full click log (timestamp, referrer, IP)
Expected traffic at launch?*

Decides whether rate limiting can live in-process or needs shared state like Redis.

Small — one instance is fine (< ~50 req/s)
Moderate — a few instances behind a load balancer
High — multi-region, redirects must stay fast under heavy load

Who can create short links?*

Decides the auth layer and what the rate limiter keys on (IP vs key vs account).

Anyone, anonymously

Registered user accounts
Internal services only (trusted network)

Changes the data model and collision handling.

Total click count only

Decides whether rate limiting can live in-process or needs shared state like Redis.

I want a REST API that shortens URLs, with rate limiting so it cannot be abused.

A few questions

So the build starts from the right assumptions.

What is this, shaped like?*

This decides the pipeline — a headless project never gets a Studio stage. Changeable later in Knowledge.

A UI app — people will look at it and click it
Headless — an API, CLI, library or service
Mixed — it has a face and a programmable surface
Who can create short links?*

Decides the auth layer and what the rate limiter keys on (IP vs key vs account).

Anyone, anonymously
Only clients with an API key
Registered user accounts
Internal services only (trusted network)
Can callers choose their own short code (vanity URLs)?*

Changes the data model and collision handling.

No — always auto-generated
Yes — optional custom alias
Yes — custom alias required
Do links ever expire?*

Drives storage cleanup and what a hit on a dead link returns.

Never — permanent
Caller sets an optional expiry
Fixed TTL for all links (e.g. 90 days)
What should be tracked when a short link is visited?*

Full logging adds a write on every redirect and possibly privacy obligations.

Nothing — just redirect
Total click count only
Full click log (timestamp, referrer, IP)
Expected traffic at launch?*

Decides whether rate limiting can live in-process or needs shared state like Redis.

Small — one instance is fine (< ~50 req/s)
Moderate — a few instances behind a load balancer
High — multi-region, redirects must stay fast under heavy load

So the build starts from the right assumptions.

When a short link is visited, which matters more?*

Permanent redirects get cached by browsers, so repeat visits can go uncounted.

Accurate click counts — every visit hits the server (302 redirect)
Fastest redirects — browsers may cache and skip counting some visits (301 redirect)
Can a link be deleted or edited after creation?*

With anonymous creation there are no accounts, so management needs a per-link secret or an admin path.

No — once created, a link is immutable and permanent
Yes — creation returns a secret token that allows deleting that link
Only an operator/admin can remove links (e.g. for abuse takedowns)
Who can read a link's click count?*
Anyone — public stats endpoint per short code
Only whoever holds the link's secret token
Nobody via the API — counts are internal only
